must_find.summary: The PutObject resource is "${aws_s3_bucket.logs.arn}*" (no slash), which matches every bucket whose name starts with acme-app-logs-<env> (e.g. acme-app-logs-prod-archive), not just this bucket's objects. Requirement 4 and the least-privilege convention need "${aws_s3_bucket.logs.arn}/*".

force_destroy = true lets `terraform destroy` (or replacing the bucket) delete the bucket and every log object, against the README rule that production data can't be removed by a plain destroy and the 1-year retention requirement.

Requirement 2 broken: the lifecycle expires current objects after 30 days, not 365, so logs are deleted after a month. Expiring before the 90-day Glacier transition also makes the rule inconsistent (S3 rejects an expiration earlier than a transition, so apply may fail).

nice_to_find.summary: Noncurrent versions expire after 30 days too, so a deleted or overwritten log loses its retained copy well before 1 year.
Multipart uploads to an SSE-KMS bucket also need kms:Decrypt on the key (only GenerateDataKey is granted); large log uploads can fail.

must_not_flag.summary: Principal "*" in the DenyInsecureTransport statement is correct (a Deny that applies to everyone without TLS); it does NOT make the bucket public.
Block Public Access has all four settings true; NOT a gap.
The KMS key with rotation and a 30-day deletion window is fine.
actions = ["s3:*"] inside the Deny statement is NOT over-permissive (it's a deny).
